description: A working-capital committee chair must authorize a supply-chain finance facility for supplier invoices and finalize the eligible balance, advance rate, legal structure, and funding controls, with input from credit risk, legal, and finance operations.

shared_context.S1: The company is considering a supply-chain finance facility for $6,000,000 of supplier invoices owed by its approved purchasing division.
shared_context.S2: Mara makes the binding decision on whether the facility may launch and on its operating terms.
shared_context.S3: The preliminary proposal assumes financing 90% of eligible invoices, with ordinary supplier recourse and no special funding or screening controls.
shared_context.S4: Under the committee's normal pre-launch procedure, Mara conducts a round-robin review with credit risk, legal, and finance operations before recording the final facility terms.

PF1.text: Elias received the completed obligor-concentration assessment this morning: the single-obligor limit leaves exactly $4,000,000 of the invoice pool eligible, and the approved advance rate for that exposure is exactly 85%; the assessment has not yet been uploaded to the credit file.

PF2.text: Nadia just received the signed anchor-buyer undertaking in a legal memo: the program must be non-recourse to suppliers, and the buyer's payment direction must be acknowledged before the first funding; she has not yet circulated the memo to the committee.

PF3.text: Jon's operations team completed a workflow test this week and confirmed that funding can be released only twice weekly, with every invoice requiring a 3-business-day hold for duplicate-invoice screening; the test result is not yet recorded in the launch checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The eligible invoice balance must be exactly $4,000,000.
The advance rate must be exactly 85%.
The facility must be non-recourse to suppliers.
Buyer payment acknowledgment must be required before first funding.
Each invoice must receive a 3-business-day duplicate-invoice screening hold.
The settlement must include a buyer-payment-acknowledgment commitment.
The settlement must include a duplicate-invoice-screening commitment.

decisive_facts.why: The public proposal supports financing the full $6,000,000 at 90%, while PF1 changes eligible_invoice_balance_usd to exactly 4,000,000 and advance_rate_percent to exactly 85%.

The preliminary terms allow ordinary supplier recourse and omit a buyer acknowledgment, while PF2 changes non_recourse_to_suppliers and buyer_payment_acknowledgment_required to true and requires the corresponding commitment.

The preliminary proposal specifies no operating cadence or screening hold, while PF3 changes funding_frequency to twice weekly, duplicate_invoice_screening_hold_days to exactly 3, and requires the duplicate-invoice-screening commitment.
